Macklemore has addressed the backlash he’s faced for his pro-Palestine speech. The singer took to the stage as Ed Sheeran’s opening act at MetLife Stadium on 5 September, where he said “Free Palestine” before performing his 2024 protest song “Hind’s Hall” which condemns Israel’s military campaign in Gaza. He also gave a speech, telling the audience he wanted people in Gaza and the occupied West Bank to know that they had not been forgotten. As a result, the Israeli-American Council launched a petition to Ed Sheeran and his management, urging the musician to remove Macklemore from the remainder of the tour. Artists such as Boy George and P!nk also spoke out, criticizing Macklemore’s comments and calling for Ed Sheeran to address the situation. Palestinian markets were being bombed a decade before 1948. Fleeing violence did not mean giving up a home. Haifa, 1938. Bombs hidden in milk cans tore through the Arab market. At least 21 Palestinians were killed on 6 July. More market bombings followed in Haifa and Jaffa. Historical accounts attribute these attacks to Irgun. A market is where a family's day becomes a meal. After the smoke cleared, people still had to eat. Still had to go out again. In April 1948, the Haganah bombarded Haifa's lower city as Palestinians crowded towards the harbour. By June, the American consul was reporting that returning Palestinians were treated as illegal entrants: only those the new authorities approved could remain. Violence drove people out. Power decided who could return. Leaving under fire was not consent to permanent dispossession.
